title: Complementary disclosures in financial networks: accounting geometry, prior-weighted uncertainty and bounded-error reports
oneLine: In synthetic financial networks, reports can identify a loss together while each gives no worst-case improvement: accounting constraints, the menu, the criterion and noise all matter.
abstract: Knowing balance-sheet totals need not identify losses after a shock. This candidate studies the remaining loss range when reports reveal selected exposures. Explicit synthetic networks exhibit reports that have no guaranteed value separately but identify the target jointly. A one-layer simplex construction isolates the role of accounting constraints and the allowed menu without requiring nonlinear loss. For affine targets and reports on a simplex, linear-programming duality gives an exact residual-width certificate, an identification criterion and a bounded-error extension. A layered family supplies magnitude formulas, a corrected prior-dependent submodularity criterion including zero-moment cases, and an exact heterogeneous-noise formula. These are model-specific mathematical results, not validation of real-bank disclosures, welfare gains or regulatory policy.
keyResults: A one-layer synthetic network has affine loss and reports that are jointly identifying but individually give no worst-case gain; allowing a direct target report changes the result.
On a simplex, affine residual width is the minimum oscillation after subtracting a linear combination of reported quantities; bounded errors add a weighted absolute-value penalty.
The layered family's expected-gain criterion includes zero-moment degeneracies; its exact product-noise formula covers all nonnegative coordinate error bounds.
evidence: Analytic constructions, proofs and explicit affine-width certificates, plus a completed producer-side run of the declared 44-instance synthetic study: 29 width stages completed, 14 remained unresolved and one was a separate zero-shock case. Its 1,878 retained queries comprise 657 checked rational witnesses, 1,207 solver-only UNSAT answers and 14 UNKNOWN answers. The frozen-package internal gate passed all 13 declared checks, including normal and optimised retained-evidence replay and negative controls. UNSAT proof objects were not independently checked. These finite results are not a prevalence estimate or unaffiliated full-experiment rerun. All three release assets were downloaded from GitHub and Zenodo and matched the frozen local bytes.

narration:
Useful together. Not alone. An Evidence Press briefing.

Suppose you know how much each bank owes and is owed, but not exactly who owes whom. After a shock, those totals may leave a range of possible losses. Which extra reports would narrow that range?

This candidate shows why the answer depends on four choices: the accounting constraints, the reports you allow, the meaning of uncertainty, and the amount of reporting error.

Here is the simplest idea. Three nonnegative shares must add to one. The loss depends on the first share, but the menu allows reports only of the other two. Either report alone can leave the full worst-case loss range. Together, they determine the missing share. Allow a direct report of that first share, and the problem changes completely.

A synthetic financial network realises this example with one interbank layer and a linear loss function. So nonlinear contagion is not necessary for reports to be complementary. The accounting constraint and the restricted menu can be enough.

The paper then gives exact linear-programming certificates for the remaining loss range in a broader affine simplex model, including bounded reporting errors. A separate layered family explains how magnitude, prior beliefs and unequal reporting precision change the results. Worst-case and average uncertainty must not be confused.

These are theoretical results for declared models. They do not show how often the effect occurs in real banks, establish welfare benefits, or validate a disclosure policy. Standard information theory and linear-programming duality remain explicit antecedents.

This is an unrefereed candidate for Evidence Press, dated the fourteenth of October, twenty twenty-six. The paper and evidence package accompany the release. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
